An ideal diode acts as a closed (short) switch when forward-biased and as an open switch when reverse-biased.
- **Forward Bias ($V > 0$):** Zero resistance, behaves like a **closed switch** ($I > 0$, $V = 0$).
- **Reverse Bias ($V < 0$):** Infinite resistance, behaves like an **open switch** ($I = 0$, $V < 0$).

**Ideal Diode Characteristics:**
```text
  I
  ^
  |          Forward (Closed Switch)
  |          |
  |          |
--+----------+--------> V
  |          |
  |    Open  |
  |    Switch
```
proTip: Emphasize that an ideal diode has zero forward voltage drop and infinite reverse resistance.
